record_type_quote: Addressing this major criticism, we conduct a large-scale, preregistered replication ﬁeld experiment in the 2016 presidential election.

targets.authors: Bryan, C.J., G.M. Walton, T. Rogers and C.S. Dweck
targets.title: Motivating voter turnout by invoking the self
targets.evidence_quote: First, the treatments were delivered via an Internet survey on the day before Election Day in order to replicate the mode and timing of treatment delivery used by Bryan et al. (2011).
targets.outcome_quote: Our experiment yields little evidence that priming subjects’ identities as a voter by using noun language increases turnout compared to verb language, even in the salient 2016 presidential election and in competitive states.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors report no support for the original positive noun-versus-verb effect, including the competitive and salient context suggested as necessary. Earlier Gerber studies are prior attempts and contextual comparisons, not targets of this experiment.

reasoning: New 2016 field experiment directly re-tests Bryan et al. (2011). The original field findings from Studies 2 and 3 are compared; recruitment and treatment delivery most closely mirror Study 3. The Bryan et al. (2016) commentary supplies criticism, not a separate empirical finding tested.
